biography: Amaury Biem was practically born in the pits. Growing up in São Paulo, his father, a former mechanic for the Opala Old Stock Race series, instilled in him a deep love for the rumble of classic engines. While other kids played football, Amaury was memorizing camshaft specs. He started karting at 12, immediately displaying a preternatural understanding of vehicle dynamics. A defining moment came at the 2018 Interlagos Karting Championship, where, despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, he carved his way through the field to finish second. This grit and determination caught the eye of a local Opala team owner, who offered him a junior driver contract. Now, at 24, Amaury is a rising star in the Opala Old Stock Race, known for his meticulous preparation and calculated risks, steadily climbing the ranks and aiming for championship glory.
drivingStyle: Amaury is a calculating and precise driver. He meticulously studies telemetry data and track maps, searching for every possible advantage. His approach to corners is smooth and controlled, prioritizing exit speed over aggressive entry. He's known for his exceptional tire management, often nursing his rubber to the end of a race while others fade. Under pressure, Amaury remains remarkably calm, rarely making mistakes and consistently delivering consistent lap times.
rivalries: Ricardo Vargas - A veteran of the Opala series, Vargas sees Amaury as an upstart trying to steal his spotlight.
Isabela Costa - Both are young talents, and their intense on-track battles have often resulted in dramatic finishes and heated post-race exchanges.
Joao Silva - Silva's aggressive driving style clashes with Amaury's calculated approach, leading to several on-track incidents and a simmering animosity.
quirks: Always wears the same faded blue racing gloves, a gift from his father.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba album before every race to calm his nerves.
Insists on personally checking the torque settings on every wheel nut before each session.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about brute force; it's about understanding the equation and solving it better than anyone else."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2022 Taruma Circuit Opala Old Stock Race after executing a daring last-lap overtake, showcasing his ability to perform under pressure and secure his first major victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 2021 Interlagos race while leading, due to a sudden downpour, a humbling experience that taught him the importance of adaptability and respecting unpredictable conditions.
